question: Can the reference pipeline separate causal next-base prediction from deliberate future leakage and keep declared sequence groups disjoint?
hypothesis: The causal reference is prefix-invariant, the future-reading control is not, and exact duplicate/reverse-complement and metadata conflict groups never cross folds.
data: Locally generated iid DNA and small explicitly constructed sequence records; no external genomic dataset.
training_budget: No optimizer or model training; bounded CPU reference evaluation only.
expected_falsifier: A causal prefix changes beyond 1e-12 in float64 CPU; a deliberately leaky control is not detected; a declared conflict pair crosses folds; any non-finite output is accepted.
scope: This smoke record does not complete the parent EVO-EXP01 training/benchmark proposal. Supplied seed-score examples are illustrative, not measured runs.
